elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "TrueLink shall defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates against any third-party claim..." — express defence duty extending to Client's affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence indemnifies "Client and its affiliates against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of" the enumerated triggers.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Prong (i): "an allegation that the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — tracks the service items actually defined in this agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Prong (iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or other Client data caused by TrueLink" — covers Client data generally, not a narrow subset.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Prong (iv): "TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Client shall promptly notify TrueLink of any such claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim" — control expressly allocated to the indemnifying party.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "Client shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 12(a) as rendered is reduced to "(i) any claim arising out of or relating to Client Content, and (ii) any violation of any state or federal law, rule or regulation by Client"; the breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default, Web Site and product-injury prongs are gone.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted prong (i) provides a TrueLink IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity for third-party claims.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification exclusion was added, and none is required; the absence is Customer-favourable so the condition does not bite.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion added, which is more favourable to Client than the fallback contemplates.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification exclusion added, so nothing to fail.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered language; the drafter expressly declined to add it.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees fallback remedy is present in the inserted or retained text.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual fees super-cap is stated; the rationale confirms it was deliberately omitted.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the inserted paragraph supplies an express defend-and-indemnify obligation for Client and its affiliates covering IP infringement of the Interface/Hosting/Support Services, TrueLink's breach of applicable law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or other Client data, and TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct, with notice, defence control and reasonable cooperation.

The narrowing of Section 12(a) to Client Content and Client's violations of law is required by the tenth preferred element, so deletion of the breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default, Web Site and product-injury prongs is within scope rather than a minimality overreach.

Fallback level remains incomplete (no procure/modify/replace, no refund, no 3× super-cap), but that is immaterial because position-completeness is achieved at the preferred level; declining to add the super-cap avoids importing a new limit on Vendor exposure.

Minimality holds: the favourable existing Section 12(b) breach-of-contract indemnity from TrueLink is retained, no survival tail, at-own-expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate was added, and no operative term is duplicated (the new triggers do not overlap the retained breach-of-Agreement prong).

Intent is preserved: no defined term is left dangling (Client Content, Interface, Hosting Services and Support Services are agreement terms), no cross-reference is broken, and no retained sentence contradicts the new indemnity; the comment is concise and cites the playbook position.
